newsitem.title: USA: Namibian Copper study improves outlook.
newsitem.headline: Namibian Copper study improves outlook.

text.p: Namibian Copper Mines Inc said Thursday the bankable feasibility study on the Haib Copper Project surpass earlier forecasts in terms of production levels and lower operating costs.
Current estimates of operating costs are $0.51 per pound with annual net operating cash flows of about $140 million, Namibian's statement said. It did not disclose the previous estimates.

The "Haib" will be the first new major mining project in the country of Namibia since its independence in 1990. When fully operational, targeted to July 1998, the project could represent up to 15 percent of Namibia's annual gross domestic product, the company said.
Namibian Copper said the current estimate of capital expenditure for completion of the project is $490 million.

Production levels for cathode copper using Roast Leach Electrowin alone are estimated to be in excess of 100,000 metric tonnes annually, said the company, noting this would place the Haib Copper Project as one of the top ten cathode copper producers in the world.
